business.content:
# Business Refinement — REQ-0001

Source revision: c94b223731ca60b9267799c1adc2238a29d69b404cb8cc9349bc653a04fcc7d6

## Confirmed information

### Business purpose and users

- **B-001** [D-0001] Littlelist users can attach an optional due date to a personal task, see that date in the task list and manage it during editing; tasks without due dates remain supported.

### Feature scope and existing product compatibility

- **B-002** [D-0002] Due dates are optional. A user can assign one during task creation or editing, display it clearly in the list, and subsequently change or remove it.
- **B-003** [D-0003] Preserve existing tasks without due dates and all existing CRUD and completion/reopening behavior.
- **B-004** [D-0004] Due dates persist across application restarts alongside existing task data.
- **B-005** [D-0005] Provide an intuitive, visually polished experience consistent with Littlelist.
- **B-006** [D-0006] Keep the change scoped to the local single-user demonstrator.

### Date eligibility and interpretation

- **B-007** [D-0007, D-0009, D-0010] Permit any valid calendar date, including past dates, today and future dates. Due dates remain optional; never reject a valid date merely because it is in the past.
- **B-008** [D-0012, D-0017, D-0020] Treat due dates as calendar dates in the device's local calendar, without timezone-related date shifts. Reject invalid calendar dates without overwriting the last valid saved value.

### Overdue presentation and completion

- **B-009** [D-0011, D-0016, D-0020] An unfinished task whose due date is before device-local today displays an explicit "Overdue" label with subtle warning styling. A task due today is not overdue. Preserve existing task ordering.
- **B-010** [D-0013, D-0018, D-0020] Completing a task retains its due date but removes overdue emphasis. Reopening restores overdue indication when applicable.

### Editing and clearing

- **B-011** [D-0014, D-0019, D-0020] Due-date editing and clearing follow existing autosave behavior. Clearing removes the optional due date. Cancel discards only unsaved or invalid drafts; previously saved changes remain saved.

## Unresolved issues

None recorded.

## Unconfirmed proposals

None recorded.

analysis.content:
# Functional Analysis — REQ-0001

Baseline: 76f0b3fbf7a093a9633e5ca10b3fc396174bde50e728c4d251ac02a03942250e
Approval: BD-0001
Handoff: 4d98af74-7793-4ab1-85b1-c822a7192d3e

## Functional requirements

### FR-001 — Optional due date and visible task date
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0002
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Allow task creation with or without an optional due date, assignment during editing, and clear display of the assigned calendar date in the task list.

### FR-002 — Edit and clear with existing autosave
Business sources: B-002, B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0019
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Allow changing or clearing an assigned due date through existing editing/autosave behavior. Cancel discards only unsaved or invalid drafts and never undoes already saved changes.

### FR-003 — Calendar date eligibility and validation
Business sources: B-007, B-008
Discovery evidence: D-0009, D-0017
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Accept past, present and future valid calendar dates. Use the device local calendar without timezone-related shifts. Reject invalid calendar dates while preserving the last valid saved date; absence of a date is valid.

### FR-004 — Overdue presentation without reordering
Business sources: B-009
Discovery evidence: D-0016
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: For an unfinished task with a date before device-local today, show an explicit Overdue label and subtle warning styling. Today, future dates and undated tasks are not overdue. Preserve existing ordering.

### FR-005 — Completion retains due dates
Business sources: B-010
Discovery evidence: D-0018
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Completing a task retains its date without overdue emphasis. Reopening restores overdue indication if the retained date is before device-local today.

### FR-006 — Durability and CRUD compatibility
Business sources: B-003, B-004
Discovery evidence: D-0003, D-0004
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Persist assigned, changed and cleared dates across restarts. Preserve existing undated records and CRUD/completion behavior.

### FR-007 — Consistent Littlelist experience
Business sources: B-005
Discovery evidence: D-0005
Status: specified
Questions: -
Statement: Present date creation, editing, clearing, display and validation as an intuitive, visually polished part of the existing Littlelist experience.

## Use cases

### UC-001 — Create task with optional date
Business sources: B-002, B-007, B-008, B-004, B-005
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0009, D-0017, D-0004, D-0005
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001, FR-003, FR-006, FR-007
Questions: -
Actor: Littlelist user
Preconditions: Littlelist is running and the user is creating a task.
Trigger: The user creates a task.
Main flow: 1. The user enters a valid task title and optionally selects a calendar date.
  2. The application validates the date when supplied.
  3. The application saves the task and shows its assigned date in the list.
Alternative flows: Leaving the date empty is valid. A past date is valid. An impossible date is rejected without being saved; existing task validation remains intact.
Outcome: The task and any selected date are available in the list and remain saved across restart.

### UC-002 — Edit, validate or clear a due date
Business sources: B-002, B-011, B-008, B-004, B-005
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0019, D-0017, D-0004, D-0005
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002, FR-003, FR-006, FR-007
Questions: -
Actor: Littlelist user
Preconditions: An existing task is available for editing.
Trigger: The user edits its due date.
Main flow: 1. The user opens the existing task editor.
  2. The user selects another date or clears the date.
  3. Valid changes follow existing autosave and update the task list.
Alternative flows: An invalid draft preserves the last valid saved date. Cancel discards only unsaved or invalid draft changes; previously autosaved changes remain saved.
Outcome: The valid new date or absence of date is saved; cancellation does not undo saved changes.

### UC-003 — View overdue state and complete or reopen
Business sources: B-002, B-009, B-010
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0016, D-0018
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001, FR-004, FR-005
Questions: -
Actor: Littlelist user
Preconditions: Tasks are available in the list, with or without dates.
Trigger: The user views tasks or changes completion state.
Main flow: 1. The application shows assigned dates and identifies unfinished tasks dated before local today as Overdue.
  2. The user completes a task; the date remains and overdue emphasis disappears.
  3. The user reopens it; overdue indication returns when applicable.
Alternative flows: Today and future dates do not cause overdue status. Undated tasks remain supported. Existing ordering does not change.
Outcome: Dates and completion-related presentation reflect the current task state without changing ordering.

## Business rules

### BR-001 — No chronological rejection
Business sources: B-007
Discovery evidence: D-0009
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-003
Questions: -
Statement: A valid calendar date must not be rejected solely because it is before today; due dates are optional.

### BR-002 — Overdue predicate
Business sources: B-009, B-010
Discovery evidence: D-0016, D-0018
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-004, FR-005
Questions: -
Statement: Overdue emphasis applies only to unfinished tasks with a due date strictly before device-local today; completed or undated tasks receive no overdue emphasis.

### BR-003 — Cancel is not rollback of saved changes
Business sources: B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0019
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Statement: Cancellation discards only the current unsaved or invalid draft; it does not revert earlier autosaved date changes.

## Acceptance criteria

### AC-001 — Create without a due date
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0002
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001
Questions: -
Given: A user is creating a task with a valid title.
When: The user leaves the due date empty and creates the task.
Then: The task is saved without a due date and remains usable.

### AC-002 — Past, today and future dates are accepted
Business sources: B-002, B-007, B-008
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0009, D-0017
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001, FR-003
Questions: -
Given: A user creates or edits a task and supplies a valid calendar date before, on or after device-local today.
When: The task or date change is saved.
Then: The selected date is accepted in all three cases; being past is never itself a rejection reason.

### AC-003 — Assigned date visible in task list
Business sources: B-002
Discovery evidence: D-0002
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-001
Questions: -
Given: A task has a saved due date.
When: The user views the task list.
Then: The assigned calendar date is clearly visible for that task.

### AC-004 — Change an existing date
Business sources: B-002, B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0019
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Given: An existing task has a saved due date.
When: The user selects another valid date and existing autosave completes.
Then: The new date replaces the old date and is shown in the list.

### AC-005 — Clear an existing date
Business sources: B-002, B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0002, D-0019
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Given: A task has a saved due date.
When: The user clears it and existing autosave completes.
Then: The date is removed; the task remains usable without a date and has no overdue indication.

### AC-006 — Invalid calendar draft preserves saved value
Business sources: B-008
Discovery evidence: D-0017
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-003
Questions: -
Given: A task has a last valid saved due date.
When: The user attempts to save an impossible calendar date.
Then: The invalid date is rejected and the last valid saved date remains unchanged.

### AC-007 — No timezone-related date shift
Business sources: B-008
Discovery evidence: D-0017
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-003
Questions: -
Given: A user selects a calendar date on a device with a local timezone different from UTC.
When: The date is saved and the task is viewed or reopened after restart.
Then: The same selected calendar date is displayed without shifting it through timezone conversion.

### AC-008 — Past unfinished task is overdue
Business sources: B-009
Discovery evidence: D-0016
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-004
Questions: -
Given: An unfinished task has a due date earlier than device-local today.
When: The user views the task list.
Then: The task shows an explicit Overdue label and subtle warning styling without changing task ordering.

### AC-009 — Today, future and undated tasks are not overdue
Business sources: B-009
Discovery evidence: D-0016
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-004
Questions: -
Given: Unfinished tasks have dates equal to today, after today, or no due date.
When: The user views the task list.
Then: None of these tasks shows overdue emphasis; ordering remains unchanged.

### AC-010 — Complete and reopen a dated task
Business sources: B-010
Discovery evidence: D-0018
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-005
Questions: -
Given: An unfinished dated task is overdue.
When: The user completes it and later reopens it.
Then: Completion retains the date and removes overdue emphasis; reopening restores it if the date is still before local today.

### AC-011 — Cancel unsaved draft retains saved changes
Business sources: B-011
Discovery evidence: D-0019
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-002
Questions: -
Given: A date change has already autosaved and the user then makes an unsaved or invalid date draft.
When: The user cancels the draft.
Then: Only that draft is discarded; the most recently autosaved date or saved cleared state remains.

### AC-012 — Dates and cleared state persist across restart
Business sources: B-004
Discovery evidence: D-0004
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-006
Questions: -
Given: Tasks include an assigned date, a changed date and a cleared date.
When: The application is stopped and restarted.
Then: Each saved date or cleared state is retained for its task.

### AC-013 — Existing undated task compatibility
Business sources: B-003
Discovery evidence: D-0003
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-006
Questions: -
Given: Existing task data was created by the original CRUD application with no due-date fields.
When: The extended application opens that data.
Then: Existing titles, descriptions and completion states remain intact and the tasks have no due date.

### AC-014 — Original CRUD and completion regression
Business sources: B-003
Discovery evidence: D-0003
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-006
Questions: -
Given: Existing tasks and newly created tasks include dated and undated examples.
When: The user creates, reads, edits, completes, reopens and confirms deletion of tasks.
Then: The existing CRUD/completion behavior remains operational, including title validation and deletion confirmation.

### AC-015 — Consistent usable date controls
Business sources: B-005
Discovery evidence: D-0005
Status: specified
Requirements: FR-007
Questions: -
Given: The user operates Littlelist in its existing desktop or phone layout.
When: The user creates or edits a date and views its display and validation state.
Then: Date controls and messages remain readable and usable, visually consistent with the existing Littlelist layout.

## Business coverage

- **B-001** [contextual] - | Purpose and users; concrete behavior is elaborated by B-002.

- **B-002** [elaborated] FR-001, FR-002 | Optional dates, task-list display, changes and clearing.

- **B-003** [elaborated] FR-006 | Retain undated records and existing CRUD/completion.

- **B-004** [elaborated] FR-006 | Durable assigned, changed and cleared dates.

- **B-005** [elaborated] FR-007 | Consistent usable Littlelist experience.

- **B-006** [contextual] - | Local single-user demonstration boundary, not a new account/platform feature.

- **B-007** [elaborated] FR-003 | Any valid calendar date is permitted.

- **B-008** [elaborated] FR-003 | Local calendar interpretation and invalid-date preservation.

- **B-009** [elaborated] FR-004 | Overdue predicate, visible label and unchanged order.

- **B-010** [elaborated] FR-005 | Date retention across completion and reopening.

- **B-011** [elaborated] FR-002 | Autosave, clearing and cancel-draft behavior.

## Inherited unresolved items

None recorded.

## Analysis questions

None recorded.

## Analysis proposals

None recorded.

payload.content:
# Test Strategy — REQ-0001

## Authority and scope

AI-authored QA draft from approved Functional Analysis baseline 63329d63c760e41f166e1b99d277534aeb8063e3469e7383a26e45ce4ad5e649 and explicit advancement faa97785-1068-4c72-9d78-e3683828ed05. The approved Business dependency is retained through that baseline. Testing skill 1.3.0, digest 86975e0917f3db19923051aeee52c367b1b5c9ceac62985190cd4a2f0594de1f. Product expectations derive only from approved FR/AC items; no Technical Design, implementation plan or prototype supplies expected outcomes. Scope: all 7 FRs and 15 ACs, local single-user Littlelist due dates and existing CRUD compatibility. No inherited unresolved items, excluded approved requirements or prototype limitations exist in this Analysis.

## Test approach

Engineering owns unit/build checks. QA will later prepare separately approved integration and real-browser UI automation; no checks have run at this design stage. Keep exact Analysis and case links, controlled data and observable assertions. Cover positive, negative, boundary and regression paths: optional/mutable dates, chronological permission, impossible dates, local-calendar/timezone stability, overdue boundaries, completion, autosave/cancel, real process restart and original undated records.

Use isolated databases and deterministic device-local clocks; test past/today/future without converting the product rule to UTC. Include desktop and phone layouts consistent with Littlelist. HTTP-only checks do not count as UI evidence; real browser actions must assert visible states. Preserve failed output, source-bound results and defects. Baseline CRUD tests are regression context, not evidence that the unimplemented feature passes.

After scenario approval, require separate advancement, approved Design interfaces, authorized QA automation preparation under qa/, separate automation approval, reviewed Engineering implementation and execution readiness before runs. No dependency installation, automation coding, Engineering edits or lifecycle advancement is authorized by this draft.

## Coverage and unresolved items

All 22 active FR/AC items have planned scenario coverage; 23 specified scenarios, none executed. Structured coverage disposition implemented means specified scenario coverage, not implemented automation or passed tests. No blocked, excluded or unresolved items; no authorized limitations. A new upstream Analysis cycle requires explicit impact reconciliation.

## Risks

<!-- Optional section; omit when not applicable. -->

The main risks are unsupported past-date rejection, timezone day shifts, midnight/year-boundary errors, invalid drafts overwriting saved values, autosave races, lost legacy records and false UI-test claims. Cases explicitly challenge these risks. Concrete API/selector/runner details await approved Design interfaces; this is an automation dependency, not an unresolved business requirement. Qualitative UI consistency requires real visual inspection alongside browser assertions; no external accessibility certification is claimed.

cases.preconditions: A user is creating a task with a valid title.

cases.expected: The selected date is accepted in all three cases; being past is never itself a rejection reason.
cases.preconditions: A user creates or edits a task and supplies a valid calendar date before, on or after device-local today.

cases.action: The user views the task list.
cases.expected: The assigned calendar date is clearly visible for that task.
cases.preconditions: A task has a saved due date.

cases.expected: The new date replaces the old date and is shown in the list.
cases.preconditions: An existing task has a saved due date.

cases.action: The user clears it and existing autosave completes.
cases.expected: The date is removed; the task remains usable without a date and has no overdue indication.
cases.preconditions: A task has a saved due date.

cases.action: The user attempts to save an impossible calendar date.
cases.expected: The invalid date is rejected and the last valid saved date remains unchanged.
cases.preconditions: A task has a last valid saved due date.

cases.action: The date is saved and the task is viewed or reopened after restart.
cases.expected: The same selected calendar date is displayed without shifting it through timezone conversion.
cases.preconditions: A user selects a calendar date on a device with a local timezone different from UTC.

cases.action: The user views the task list.
cases.expected: The task shows an explicit Overdue label and subtle warning styling without changing task ordering.
cases.preconditions: An unfinished task has a due date earlier than device-local today.

cases.action: The user views the task list.
cases.expected: None of these tasks shows overdue emphasis; ordering remains unchanged.
cases.preconditions: Unfinished tasks have dates equal to today, after today, or no due date.

cases.action: The user completes it and later reopens it.
cases.expected: Completion retains the date and removes overdue emphasis; reopening restores it if the date is still before local today.
cases.preconditions: An unfinished dated task is overdue.

cases.action: The user cancels the draft.
cases.expected: Only that draft is discarded; the most recently autosaved date or saved cleared state remains.
cases.preconditions: A date change has already autosaved and the user then makes an unsaved or invalid date draft.

cases.action: The application is stopped and restarted.
cases.expected: Each saved date or cleared state is retained for its task.
cases.preconditions: Tasks include an assigned date, a changed date and a cleared date.

cases.action: The extended application opens that data.

cases.preconditions: Existing task data was created by the original CRUD application with no due-date fields.

cases.expected: Date controls and messages remain readable and usable, visually consistent with the existing Littlelist layout.
cases.preconditions: The user operates Littlelist in its existing desktop or phone layout.

cases.action: Create and edit tasks using yesterday, today and tomorrow, independently through the actual UI and the supported integration boundary.
cases.expected: All valid dates are accepted and remain the selected calendar dates. No minimum-today restriction prevents past-date entry.
cases.preconditions: Run with a controlled device-local today and a task without a date.

cases.action: Save the valid leap-day value, then attempt impossible February dates through the supported data-entry and integration boundary.

# Test Scenarios — REQ-0001

## Authority

AI-authored QA draft from approved Functional Analysis baseline 63329d63c760e41f166e1b99d277534aeb8063e3469e7383a26e45ce4ad5e649 and explicit advancement faa97785-1068-4c72-9d78-e3683828ed05. The approved Business dependency is retained through that baseline. Testing skill 1.3.0, digest 86975e0917f3db19923051aeee52c367b1b5c9ceac62985190cd4a2f0594de1f. Product expectations derive only from approved FR/AC items; no Technical Design, implementation plan or prototype supplies expected outcomes. Scope: all 7 FRs and 15 ACs, local single-user Littlelist due dates and existing CRUD compatibility. No inherited unresolved items, excluded approved requirements or prototype limitations exist in this Analysis.

## Scenarios

### TC-001 — Create without a due date
References: FR-001, AC-001
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A user is creating a task with a valid title.
Action: The user leaves the due date empty and creates the task.
Expected: The task is saved without a due date and remains usable.

### TC-002 — Past, today and future dates are accepted
References: FR-001, FR-003, AC-002
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A user creates or edits a task and supplies a valid calendar date before, on or after device-local today.
Action: The task or date change is saved.
Expected: The selected date is accepted in all three cases; being past is never itself a rejection reason.

### TC-003 — Assigned date visible in task list
References: FR-001, AC-003
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A task has a saved due date.
Action: The user views the task list.
Expected: The assigned calendar date is clearly visible for that task.

### TC-004 — Change an existing date
References: FR-002, AC-004
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: An existing task has a saved due date.
Action: The user selects another valid date and existing autosave completes.
Expected: The new date replaces the old date and is shown in the list.

### TC-005 — Clear an existing date
References: FR-002, AC-005
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A task has a saved due date.
Action: The user clears it and existing autosave completes.
Expected: The date is removed; the task remains usable without a date and has no overdue indication.

### TC-006 — Invalid calendar draft preserves saved value
References: FR-003, AC-006
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A task has a last valid saved due date.
Action: The user attempts to save an impossible calendar date.
Expected: The invalid date is rejected and the last valid saved date remains unchanged.

### TC-007 — No timezone-related date shift
References: FR-003, AC-007
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A user selects a calendar date on a device with a local timezone different from UTC.
Action: The date is saved and the task is viewed or reopened after restart.
Expected: The same selected calendar date is displayed without shifting it through timezone conversion.

### TC-008 — Past unfinished task is overdue
References: FR-004, AC-008
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: An unfinished task has a due date earlier than device-local today.
Action: The user views the task list.
Expected: The task shows an explicit Overdue label and subtle warning styling without changing task ordering.

### TC-009 — Today, future and undated tasks are not overdue
References: FR-004, AC-009
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: Unfinished tasks have dates equal to today, after today, or no due date.
Action: The user views the task list.
Expected: None of these tasks shows overdue emphasis; ordering remains unchanged.

### TC-010 — Complete and reopen a dated task
References: FR-005, AC-010
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: An unfinished dated task is overdue.
Action: The user completes it and later reopens it.
Expected: Completion retains the date and removes overdue emphasis; reopening restores it if the date is still before local today.

### TC-011 — Cancel unsaved draft retains saved changes
References: FR-002, AC-011
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A date change has already autosaved and the user then makes an unsaved or invalid date draft.
Action: The user cancels the draft.
Expected: Only that draft is discarded; the most recently autosaved date or saved cleared state remains.

### TC-012 — Dates and cleared state persist across restart
References: FR-006, AC-012
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: Tasks include an assigned date, a changed date and a cleared date.
Action: The application is stopped and restarted.
Expected: Each saved date or cleared state is retained for its task.

### TC-013 — Existing undated task compatibility
References: FR-006, AC-013
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: Existing task data was created by the original CRUD application with no due-date fields.
Action: The extended application opens that data.
Expected: Existing titles, descriptions and completion states remain intact and the tasks have no due date.

### TC-014 — Original CRUD and completion regression
References: FR-006, AC-014
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: Existing tasks and newly created tasks include dated and undated examples.
Action: The user creates, reads, edits, completes, reopens and confirms deletion of tasks.
Expected: The existing CRUD/completion behavior remains operational, including title validation and deletion confirmation.

### TC-015 — Consistent usable date controls
References: FR-007, AC-015
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: The user operates Littlelist in its existing desktop or phone layout.
Action: The user creates or edits a date and views its display and validation state.
Expected: Date controls and messages remain readable and usable, visually consistent with the existing Littlelist layout.

### TC-016 — Past, today and future dates are accepted
References: FR-001, FR-003, AC-002
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: Run with a controlled device-local today and a task without a date.
Action: Create and edit tasks using yesterday, today and tomorrow, independently through the actual UI and the supported integration boundary.
Expected: All valid dates are accepted and remain the selected calendar dates. No minimum-today restriction prevents past-date entry.

### TC-017 — Invalid calendar draft preserves saved value
References: FR-003, AC-006
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: An existing task has a valid saved due date. Use controlled fixtures containing 2024-02-29, 2025-02-29 and 2024-02-30.
Action: Save the valid leap-day value, then attempt impossible February dates through the supported data-entry and integration boundary.
Expected: The valid leap day saves. Impossible dates do not replace it. Validation communicates failure rather than claiming a save.

### TC-018 — No timezone-related date shift
References: FR-003, AC-007
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: Run equivalent date-entry fixtures in device timezones Pacific/Kiritimati and America/Los_Angeles, with the same selected calendar date.
Action: Create, save, reload and edit the date, including a fixture near a daylight-saving transition.
Expected: The selected calendar date never shifts forward or backward because of timezone conversion; no time-of-day meaning is introduced.

### TC-019 — Past unfinished task is overdue
References: FR-004, AC-008
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: Use two unfinished task fixtures around a controlled local year boundary: 31 December and 1 January.
Action: View the task list on 1 January device-local today.
Expected: 31 December is overdue; 1 January is not. Existing creation order remains unchanged.

### TC-020 — Today, future and undated tasks are not overdue
References: FR-004, AC-009
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A task is due on device-local today; the test clock can advance to the following local day.
Action: View the list before midnight, advance the controlled local calendar day, then view the list again.
Expected: The date remains unchanged. It is not overdue on its due day and is overdue when viewed as unfinished the next day; no requirement for a background timer is invented.

### TC-021 — Complete and reopen a dated task
References: FR-005, AC-010
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A task has a past due date and can be shown in the existing Active, Completed and All views.
Action: Complete it, inspect the completed task date, reopen it and inspect its overdue state.
Expected: The date is retained across completion and reopening. Completed presentation has no overdue emphasis; reopening restores it without reordering.

### TC-022 — Cancel unsaved draft retains saved changes
References: FR-002, AC-011
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: A task has an autosaved date change; separately exercise a task whose date was already cleared and saved.
Action: Enter an unsaved valid date draft or an invalid draft and cancel before it is saved.
Expected: The latest saved changed date or cleared state is preserved. Cancel does not restore an older date or save the draft.

### TC-023 — Dates and cleared state persist across restart
References: FR-006, AC-012
Status: specified; not automated or executed.
Preconditions: Prepare dated and cleared tasks with active/completed states using an isolated database.
Action: Stop the actual application process, restart with the same database, and inspect the saved task states through the UI and integration boundary.
Expected: Each date or absence of date, along with existing task identity/content/completion, survives restart. No personal database is used.

## Coverage and unresolved items

All 22 active FR/AC items have planned scenario coverage; 23 specified scenarios, none executed. Structured coverage disposition implemented means specified scenario coverage, not implemented automation or passed tests. No blocked, excluded or unresolved items; no authorized limitations. A new upstream Analysis cycle requires explicit impact reconciliation.

## Test data

<!-- Optional section; omit when not applicable. -->

Fictional tasks, controlled device-local today, yesterday/today/tomorrow, month/year boundaries, valid and invalid February dates, positive/negative UTC offset and DST fixtures, active/completed and dated/undated tasks, saved/unsaved/invalid drafts, isolated SQLite-compatible legacy task records. Exact automation mechanics follow approved interfaces; no product date range restriction is introduced.
